rule: Four open clauses of the campaign's success criteria were blocked on a ruling no implementation lane may write, and that fact was scattered across a report section, three escalation ledgers and a verify-ledger note. Scattered, it reads as four lanes each explaining why it stopped. Collected, it is one list with a length: these are the decisions the campaign owed itself, and nothing below closed by anybody trying harder. Every row names the criterion it blocked, the artifact carrying the measurement, the question in one sentence, and what a lane may NOT do instead -- because the second half is what keeps 'blocked on a ruling' from becoming the place work goes to stop. The first four were answered on 2026-08-14 by dated amendments in the umbrella; the rows moved to answered[] rather than being deleted, so the question, its measurement and its answer stay joined. A fifth was opened the same day, by the pass that closed the other four: a criterion cannot be discharged by the lane that discovers it is unmet. A sixth was opened by the pass that docketed the standing dissents, for the same reason and from the other end -- the one debt whose remedy is not an investigation, found by asking what a fresh investigator would be asked and finding no question; it was answered on 2026-08-15 by Amendment J, which adjudicates such a string by source assertion, and its row moved to answered[] rather than being deleted. A seventh was opened on the same day by the pass that sized the fourteen receipt-walk deferrals into slices: three of them name a retiring act the campaign's own criterion 8 forbids, which is a mis-description of a debt rather than a debt anybody can pay. The seventh was answered on 2026-08-15 by Amendment K, which rules the retiring act per LANE rather than per walk -- the interpreter in the family's own declared serving lane, which is the receipt walk for eleven of the rows and the defence resolver for the three whose via says so -- and its row moved to answered[] rather than being deleted. An eighth was opened on 2026-08-16 by the retirement lane that measured a family with no pair row to stamp, and answered the same day by Amendment O, which rules such a family PAIR_ONLY under the umbrella's own semantic-authority rule and closes its receipt-walk row as a schedule category error rather than a retirement -- with a machine check that reopens it, and with a one-pass triage of every remaining row so the sixth lane does not rediscover what stopped the fifth; its row moved to answered[] rather than being deleted. A ninth was opened on 2026-08-16 by the next retirement lane and from the opposite end of the same debt: three rows whose ruled retiring act is not missing but ALREADY PERFORMED, in a lane the deferral row is not keyed on, so no amount of doing the ruled act could ever move them. It was answered the same day by Amendment Q, which rules that a family whose walk-side need is served through its declared lane must not declare a receipt-walk lane at all, closes the three rows as lane-declaration corrections carrying a machine check in both directions and a reopening condition, and moved its row to answered[] rather than being deleted. A tenth was opened on 2026-08-16 by the retirement lane that reached the first family whose packet is DELIVERED AS A BASIC ATTACK SWING: the budgeted pricing stage carries a resistance and the holder's amps, and a swing meets three further target-side terms of which one -- a capped flat subtraction applied per crit outcome before the blend -- is not a factor any declared magnitude can carry, while the family's second authored row declares no magnitude at all and re-delivers another family's. It was answered the same day by Amendment R, which rules the swing composition onto the stage with the subtraction carried and never folded, widens the term census's predicate to authoring-time terms so the next such term is measured rather than tripped over, rules that a routing family declares no magnitude of its own, and orders a covering scenario that arms the enemy-held terms as an integration act; its row moved to answered[] rather than being deleted. That leaves one row open, and it is the first one: whether criterion 11's first clause binds the campaign backwards. Corrected 2026-08-18: the sentence above ends 'That leaves one row open, and it is the first one', which was true when it was written and is not true of this file. It was answered on 2026-08-17 by the campaign owner -- the fixed-point reading, recorded in the umbrella's Owner's rulings section rather than as an amendment, because no re-reading by the orchestration could have reached it -- and its row moved to answered[] rather than being deleted. The sentence stays written because a justification that is only deleted is one no reader can check was ever real. owed[] is now empty, and an empty owed list is a state this ledger was built to reach rather than one that empties its own checks: every join here ranges over owed and answered together, and the measurement gate follows the row that carries the measurement rather than the list it sits in.
how_a_row_closes: The ruling is recorded in docs/plans/2026-08-08-silent-failure-campaign.md -- in the [H] table, in a decision row, or as a dated amendment, which is where Amendments A through D already live -- and the row moves to answered[] naming the amendment. A row does NOT close by a lane deciding the question is smaller than it looked, and it does not close by the criterion being re-read more weakly: umbrella criterion 11's own words are that a phase document may not write its own descope. Extended 2026-08-18 by the tenth closure, which is the first that no amendment could carry: a ruling that is the campaign OWNER's is recorded in the umbrella's 'Owner's rulings' section, dated and naming this row's id, and the row moves to answered[] naming it in the same field the amendments use. The section exists so the two are distinguishable in the tree: an amendment is the orchestration re-reading its own contract, and an owner's ruling is an answer to a question the orchestration was forbidden to give itself.
why_a_lane_may_not_write_these: Umbrella criterion 11: every [H] is either answered and recorded in the umbrella or its dependent slice is explicitly descoped there with its criterion restated -- a phase document may not write its own descope. The same reasoning reaches a success criterion an implementation would have to reinterpret to satisfy. Amendments A, B, C and D are the precedent: each was measured by a lane, refused by that lane, and recorded in the umbrella by its owner.

answered.amendment: Amendment E — 2026-08-14, how a disposition transition is adjudicated
answered.the_ruling: A disposition transition is adjudicated BY CITATION, not by verdict, under three guards: the diff must be on a dispositions entry as the identity-keyed leaf_report classifies it; the cited ruling must be one a reader can open; and the leaf the entry describes may not move. The third guard is this amendment's own contribution -- citation can only ever excuse a change in what a payload SAYS ABOUT a number that did not change.

Umbrella criterion 1's emission clause.

answered.the_ruling: Criterion 4 carves out a leaf's own adjudicating receipt on three conditions: the restatement sits inside an artifact adjudicating that exact leaf, it names the leaf by its path, and it agrees with the committed receipt or declares in the same artifact what it supersedes. A quotation at its address is the opposite of a second home; a second home is a figure a reader cannot trace.

answered.amendment: Amendment J — 2026-08-15, how a campaign-authored justification string is adjudicated
answered.the_ruling: A campaign-authored justification string that asserts a fact about src-level vocabulary is adjudicated BY SOURCE ASSERTION -- a machine check binding the string to the predicate that produces it -- and never by an R-18 investigation, whose export excludes src/ by design. An oracle verdict on such a string is valid only for its export-verifiable portion, so a verdict that turns on a vocabulary its own limitations block declares out of bounds does not sustain a dissent; and the string MAY assert the src-vocabulary fact, because the machine check is what keeps it true. Three guards: one named producing site rather than a hand list, a check total over what the sentence quantifies over and in both directions, and nothing carved out but the src-vocabulary claim -- whatever such a string asserts about the cached corpus stays R-18's.

The investigator checked both sentences against the cached corpus, found the operative claim supported on BOTH sides, and certified the old value -- because R-19's closed verdict set has no member for 'both are true and the evidence tree does not rank them'. Is a campaign-authored justification string adjudicated by citation on the same reasoning, or does R-19's verdict set gain a member for a leaf the export cannot rank?
answered.what_the_ruling_unblocked: The one docketed dissent no investigation could clear. oracle-P3-3.8-leaf24.json stands exactly as filed and is answered rather than superseded; its open_debt row closes as a citation naming Amendment J, the docket cluster routed here leaves clusters[] by being answered, and the twenty-three-receipt majority is not re-rolled. What lands is the ruling's premise made enforceable: the source assertion binding the published sentence to item_coverage.declares_only_defence, over every cached item and in both directions, so the day the defence group changes under the sentence a gate goes red rather than a receipt going stale.

answered.amendment: Amendment K — 2026-08-15, the retiring act is named per lane, not per walk
answered.the_ruling: The retiring act for every one of the fourteen (family, RECEIPT_WALK) deferral rows is a per-family interpreter in the family's OWN DECLARED SERVING LANE -- RECEIPT_WALK for the eleven the pair engine feeds, DEFENSE_RESOLVER for the three the resolver feeds, and in general whichever lane that row's via names. Amendment F's act is neither narrowed nor widened; what is corrected is the lane it was spelled with, which was read off eleven rows and written over fourteen. One property is discharged either way and it is criterion 8's own: the family's numbers reach the walk through exactly one interpreter, in the lane the family declares, instead of arriving already priced by the pair engine -- so the act serves D-60 rather than colliding with it, because a resolver interpreter is not a second producer of one number, it is the one producer. delta_amp is answered by the same sentence: its structured via is pair_engine, so its ruled act is a receipt-walk interpreter, and prose naming a second route does not move a gated declaration (D-40). Three refusals ride the ruling: no interpreter is registered that emits fields nothing consumes, _FAMILY_LANES is not touched so counter 4 still counts all three, and Amendment F's fourteen are not read as eleven. The rows' recorded retiring stage is refreshed from 'Phase 4 S3 -- one kernel, five views', which Amendment F measured cannot perform the act, to this closeout, dated and citing Amendment F; re-dating changes what the rows are overdue AGAINST and nothing about whether they are overdue.

What retires them: an interpreter the criterion forbids, a lane-table correction saying the receipt walk never owed this family its own answer, or something else -- and does the same answer reach delta_amp, whose structured route says pair_engine while its own reason names a second route and says neither is the rule?

What it deliberately did NOT unblock is the debt: INTERPRETERS already holds the three (family, DEFENSE_RESOLVER) keys, so for those three the ruled act is already performed and the one-engine property is discharged today -- a fact about the tree and not permission to stop counting. All fourteen rows stand, overdue and gated, the machine still refuses a fifteenth, and the eleven are still eleven slices no phase has budgeted.

Every remaining row now carries a measured class instead of an unmeasured assumption: four author their own rows and retire by the ruled act, five fold into rows they do not author, and one of those five -- damage_routing -- has no named walk-side delivery term anywhere in the tree or in an amendment, so the next retirement round stops there by name rather than by a sixth lane rediscovering the shape that stopped the fifth. answered.amendment: Amendment Q — 2026-08-16, the lane a served walk-side need does not owe
answered.the_ruling: LANE-DECLARATION CORRECTION. A family whose walk-side need is satisfied THROUGH its declared serving lane does not need -- and must not declare -- a RECEIPT_WALK interpreter lane: one producer is precisely what the one-engine thesis demands, so a table that goes on asking a second lane for an answer the first lane already gives is asking for the thing criterion 8 forbids, and the deferral row underneath it is counting the absence of a defect. RECEIPT_WALK leaves _FAMILY_LANES for exactly the three measured families the defence resolver feeds, on the measured ground, in Amendment O, Ruling 1's shape -- WITH a machine check in BOTH directions and a reopening condition. Forwards: the named walk-side implementation reads the resolver's resolved state, source-asserted, derived per declaration rather than asserted per family, and a declaration nothing consumes fails the gate by name. Backwards: deleting the family's resolver interpreter flips its items to WITHHELD with a receipt naming the missing (family, defense_resolver) pair, never to a silent zero, run over every declaring owner on every check with an R-05 negative proving the red. Reopening: if a mechanic of one of these families ever authors walk-priced rows not fed by the resolver, the lane re-enters and the row reopens. This is not D-40's prohibition, because the declaration is corrected on a measured ground recorded in the umbrella with its check rather than edited to move a counter -- the walk consumes this family's numbers from the lane the family declares, and that is measured before the table moves and stays measured after it. Amendment K's three refusals stand as written: no interpreter is registered that emits fields nothing consumes, Amendment F's fourteen are not read as eleven, and what changes is a declaration that was wrong rather than a debt that was owed.

INTERPRETERS has held all three of those keys since before the closeout opened, so the ruled act is performed. The deferral row is a different object: scripts/behavior_frontier.py derives counter 4's rows from interpreters.uninterpreted_pairs(), so combat_state/receipt_walk retires when and only when that pair leaves that tuple, which an interpreter registered in another lane does not do and cannot do. So what retires it? Either the receipt-walk lane declaration comes out of _FAMILY_LANES on the measured ground that the family's delivery is performed in the lane it declares -- an Amendment O, Ruling 1 shaped act on a different ground, owing its own machine check and its own reopening condition -- or the rows close on some further ground the umbrella names, as Amendment O closed crit_profile's on a ground that was not a retirement at all.

What it deliberately did NOT unblock is the debt: five rows stand, overdue and gated, none of them budgeted, the machine still refuses a sixth, no interpreter is registered and no walk begins pricing anything it did not price. Amendment F's fourteen are not read as eleven: three rows leave as mis-declared and say so in their own words, which is a correction to a declaration and not a discount on a debt.

answered.amendment: Amendment R — 2026-08-16, the basic-attack swing terms, the census's reach, and a routed magnitude's owner
answered.the_ruling: FOUR RULINGS. (1) THE SWING TERMS. The from-declaration pricing stage gains the basic-attack swing composition, in the order the pair engine applies it: the packet is mitigated at ITS OWN resistance (Amendment N, Ruling 1), composed with the holder's static amps pre-mitigation (Amendment M, Ruling 1, already carried), then met by the target-side terms. Two of the three FOLD, because a pure factor on a linear mitigation composes into the declared magnitude and prices to the same real number -- the target's critical-strike damage multiplier and the plating multiplier. Warden's Mail's Rock Solid is NEVER folded: min(flat, per_hit * cap) is a capped flat SUBTRACTION and not a factor on a magnitude, it is applied to the crit branch and the non-crit branch separately BEFORE the deterministic blend, and it is carried as a term of its own -- the flat, its cap and its instance count transported on the declaration and subtracted per branch, floored at zero, before the branches are blended. The term rides ON the declaration, transported from the authored ledger rather than resolved again at the walk, for the reason Amendment N gave for the resistance; a declaration no basic-attack swing delivered carries none and prices exactly as today, so no retired family's number moves. Equivalence fixtures are seeded from the measured Caitlyn probe, BOTH inert and armed, on the reasoning that made Amendment M's fixtures cover amp != 1.0 and Amendment N's cover both windows. (2) THE CENSUS WIDENING. Amendment N, Ruling 2's census ranges over post-authoring packet mutation and the holder-amp folds beside it, and no census in that shape can reach a term applied while the packet is being AUTHORED; its prior green is recorded as TRUTHFUL under the old predicate, a fact about the census's reach rather than a defect in it. The predicate widens to range over AUTHORING-TIME mitigation terms as well -- every term _mitigate and _mitigate_basic_attack_swing apply, target-side as well as holder-side -- under the gate it already carries, with its R-05 negative updated so an injected authoring-time term turns it red, and no further family retires while the census shows an uncovered term. (3) ROUTING-FAMILY MAGNITUDE OWNERSHIP. secondary_target is a ROUTING family: it re-delivers SOURCE families' declared magnitudes at a second subject and declares no magnitude of its own (D-60, one producer per number). The copied packet is priced from the source family's declaration composed with the router's declared damage_share and attributed under D-62 at (source mechanic, secondary subject, event_id) -- the subject being what keeps that key clear of the same source mechanic's primary delivery -- with the routing recorded in provenance. The router's declaration carries exactly the routing facts it carries today, max_targets and damage_share, and gains no magnitude field. (4) COVERAGE. By integration act (R-12, R-32), the covering scenario set gains a scenario arming the enemy-held swing terms -- a defender holding Warden's Mail, with the plating multiplier and the crit-damage reduction in reach, met by an attacker whose delivery is a basic-attack swing -- and the coverage derivation READS the term mapping, the way repricing_window_declarations already reads the window mapping, so a further target-side swing term no scenario arms fails the capture on the commit that declares it. Armed means met: the mapping is a two-sided join, the defender's declaration on one side and a basic-attack delivery on the other.
answered.blocks: umbrella criterion 7 through counter 4's secondary_target/receipt_walk deferral row, and umbrella Amendment F's eighth remaining slice behind it
answered.measurement_artifact: docs/receipts/expected-golden-diff-campaign-close-secondary-target-retirement.json, the R-20 receipt of the stopped slice
answered.question: The tenth retirement attempt is the first whose family authors a packet DELIVERED AS A BASIC ATTACK SWING, and the from-declaration pricing stage cannot price one. Every family retired so far reaches the target through damage._mitigate and nothing else -- a resistance and the holder's magic amp, exactly what survival.pricing.price_declared_packet carries. Runaan's Wind's Fury bolt is priced by damage._mitigate_basic_attack_swing, which applies three further terms: the holder's basic amp, which the stage carries; the target's critical-strike damage multiplier, which is a pure factor and folds; and damage._apply_target_basic_damage_reduction's plating multiplier, which folds, beside a CAPPED FLAT SUBTRACTION which does not. min(flat, per_hit * cap) is not a factor on a magnitude, and in the deterministic reading it is applied to the crit branch and the non-crit branch separately before they are blended, so the cap bites on one and not the other. Measured on a Caitlyn holding Runaan's Hurricane and Blade of the Ruined King: the declaration prices to 76.54166666666666, which is exactly the pair engine's own figure while the three terms are inert, and the pair engine reads 63.60666666666666 once Warden's Mail's declared Rock Solid is armed on the defender -- 20.3 percent, on a term no committed coupled scenario arms. A SECOND question rides with it and is the same slice's: the family's other authored row, on_hit_secondary_Runaan's Hurricane, is the attack's on-hit effects copied onto the bolt's target, and runaans_hurricane.secondary_target declares two numbers -- max_targets and damage_share -- neither of which is a magnitude for it. Its magnitudes are the already-retired on_hit_strike family's own declarations delivered at a second subject. What does the pricing stage owe a basic-attack-delivered packet, and which family declares a copied on-hit packet's magnitude?
answered.what_the_ruling_unblocked: The one row of the nine that was startable by nobody. secondary_target/receipt_walk stays OPEN, overdue and gated -- the ruling retires nothing and reads the debt as no smaller -- but the two things that stopped it are settled: the pricing stage now has a ruled shape for a basic-attack-delivered packet, including the one term that is genuinely not a factor, and the family's second authored row has a ruled owner for its magnitudes. What the stopped lane may NOT do is unchanged and is now unnecessary: it does not fold a price back out, does not refuse an armed packet, does not stamp one of two rows, and does not amend the pricing stage on its own authority, because the amendment is here. Two further consequences are carried rather than left implied: Amendment N, Ruling 2's census widens so this class of missing term is measured rather than tripped over by the next family, and Ruling 4's covering scenario is owed as an integration act before the retirement can be seen by either baseline -- measured on the ruling's own commit, Rock Solid is armed by no committed coupled scenario and by no bench roster at all.

answered.amendment: Owner's ruling — 2026-08-17, criterion 11's first clause: the fixed-point reading
answered.the_ruling: THE FIXED-POINT READING, and it takes none of the three branches the question and the close report put in front of it. Ruling 1: the clause BINDS BACKWARDS for implementation slices -- units of work that change behaviour in src/, tests/, scripts/ or data/ -- and is DISCHARGED for them by the verdicts recorded in docs/receipts/verify-ledger.json: the fresh R-35 passes, and equally the verdicts the campaign rendered and never filed, transcribed through that ledger's own backfill and residue_sweep route. A transcription of a verifier's rendered answer is that verifier's artifact reaching the ledger late; reconstructing an answer out of the commit bodies of the lanes being checked is a different act and stays forbidden. Ruling 2: verification, certification, transcription and receipt-only passes are INSTRUMENTS, not subjects. Their own ledger row -- or the certifier's signed verdict, for the terminal pass -- is their record, and they do not enter the coverage denominator. This closes the self-referential regress close-report section 16.3 measured, by which each certification pass added its own unverifiable tag to the counter it was convened to grade, and it closes it at the reading rather than at the counter. The denominator derivation is corrected to implementation-slice tags, with instrument-pass tags enumerated separately BESIDE THEIR SELF-RECORDS and under a machine check with a reproducible red: the self-record must resolve in the artifact it names, and an instrument tag whose commits touch src/ fails, because production behaviour makes a pass a subject whatever it calls itself. This is the owner's recorded ruling with its check and not a D-40 exclusion: D-40 forbids editing what a counter counts in order to move it, and what is ruled here is what the counter's unit always was, by the one party entitled to say. The three shortcuts this row refuses stay refused, the second of them in its own terms. Ruling 3: campaign-close-verify-p4-batch, the one range no verifier ever reached, is VERIFIED rather than reclassified -- it is a transcription pass that Ruling 2 could have excused, and its prepared backlog row is handed to a fresh R-35 pass instead, because a ruling whose first use is to excuse the one thing it could excuse is a ruling nobody should trust. Ruling 4: every NOT_DISCHARGED ledger row carries a disposition -- fixed citing the fix commit, superseded by later work citing that work, or documented_open carrying the artifact that holds the open debt -- while a verdict stays the verifier's and is never re-graded by a lane. Ruling 5: untagged commits that touch no behaviour are outside 'every slice'; the untagged commits that touch src/ are enumerated, derived rather than authored, and each is covered by a batch verdict naming its range or by a dated acceptance note. No commit subject is rewritten to reach that -- retro-tagging rewrites the history the denominator is derived from, and this ruling does not unrefuse it.

answered.question: The clause has a machine denominator now and fails it backwards: 68 slice-group tags derived from commit subjects, one covered by a verdict recorded in this ledger, seven more citing a verdict in their own commit bodies with a sha a reader can open, and 61 citing nothing anywhere. R-35 was real and used -- the campaign answered NOT DISCHARGED verdicts by name -- but the verdicts were written into commit bodies rather than into an artifact, so most of them are unrecoverable as records. Does the clause bind the campaign's own past, in which case somebody schedules 61 fresh R-35 passes over closed ranges; or is it discharged forwards, by a ledger whose gate refuses the next slice group that ships without a verdict row or an explicit line?
answered.what_the_ruling_unblocked: The campaign's one certification blocker, and the counter that could not stop growing. Four certification reviews withheld sign-off on this clause and each of them, by existing, added a tag to the residue it was grading; Ruling 2 ends that as a property rather than by anybody working differently, which is what the_cost_of_deciding_late measured and asked whoever ruled to weigh. What it does NOT unblock is criterion 11 itself: the clause is not discharged here. Ruling 3's fresh R-35 pass over the unreached batch range and Ruling 5's enumeration of the untagged src-touching commits are work that has to land, the residue is whatever the ledger's coverage block says it is on the tip a reader measures at -- live_figures names it rather than this row stating it -- and the clause's other two halves are untouched. What is unblocked is that every remaining step is now work a lane may do, with an owner's reading behind it, instead of a question a lane was forbidden to answer.
answered.why_no_lane_may_answer_it: Both ways out are a lane deciding what a criterion means. Reading it forwards is a re-reading of 'every slice', which criterion 11's own words forbid a phase document from doing; reading it backwards commits somebody to sixty-one verification passes, which is a scheduling decision with a cost and an owner.
answered.what_a_lane_may_not_do_instead: Three things, and each has been available and refused. Manufacture a verdict for a slice nobody verified -- that is precisely the unverifiable claim about the past Phase 1 outlaws. Reconstruct verdicts from the commit bodies of the very lanes being checked, which is a record derived from the thing it is supposed to check independently. And shrink the denominator by declaring some tags 'not really slices', which is driving a counter to zero by editing what it counts.
answered.consequence_of_leaving_it_open: The clause holds forwards and is measured backwards. The gate refuses the next slice group that ships with neither a verdict row nor an explicit line, so the residue is a number that cannot grow in silence; what it does not do is fall. What preparation changed is the cost of the branch, not the choice: whoever rules may now read the exact passes the backwards reading buys, one row each, instead of an estimate. Corrected 2026-08-17: the clause 'what it does not do is fall' was true when it was written and is not true of the tree. It fell -- 118 to 2 over three days -- and the sentence stays written because a justification that is only deleted is one no reader can check was ever real. What it correctly says is the half about growth, which still holds: the forward gate refuses the next slice group that ships with neither a verdict row nor an explicit line, and that is what has not changed. Where the number now stands is what_the_measurement_now_reads, read from the artifact rather than restated here, so this field cannot be the second home that goes stale a second time. Corrected again 2026-08-17, and it is the dated figure rather than the clause: 'It fell -- 118 to 2 over three days' dates the 118 to the wrong day and reverses what the three days did. Read out of this file's own measurement artifact, commit by commit -- git show <sha>:docs/receipts/verify-ledger.json, coverage.residue -- the residue was 62 at c029024 and 76 at a323202, both 2026-08-14; 118 is the highest reading in the ledger's history and it is 9961bf2's, on 2026-08-17, the commit before the backfill; 2 is 0be8f37's, later the same day. So the residue ROSE 62 -> 118 over the three days as the denominator grew with every slice group that shipped, and the whole of the fall 118 -> 2 is inside 2026-08-17. Both sentences stay written for the same reason the first correction gives, and the trajectory is recorded here rather than re-worded above.
answered.what_a_lane_may_do_and_has_done: Price the branch it may not choose. The backwards reading commits somebody to a number of fresh R-35 passes, and until 2026-08-14 that number was an estimate over a population nobody had turned into work: no commit range, no criteria locator and no brief existed for a single one of them. docs/receipts/verify-backlog.json, gated by tests/test_verify_backlog.py, is one prepared row per residue group -- the commits it spans by subject, the plan documents its stated completion criteria live in, and R-35's brief read from the runbook rather than copied, so a prepared pass cannot be handed a weakened one. This is a statement about the QUESTION a verifier would be asked and never about the answer, which is the same line the standing-dissent docket draws. It does not narrow the ruling: both branches remain exactly as written, and the row set is asserted equal to the ledger's own residue list so preparation cannot become redefinition.
answered.what_the_measurement_now_reads: Added 2026-08-17, and it answers nothing. The question above states its population as it stood on 2026-08-14 -- 68 tags, one covered, seven citing a verdict in a commit body, 61 citing nothing anywhere -- and that sentence is the one figure in this system with no gate keeping it current, which a verifier filed as a standing aside against this very row. The row's measurement artifact is the ledger's coverage block, so the honest fix is to read it rather than to re-word the question. Measured on this tip: 125 slice tags derived from commit subjects, 123 with a verdict recorded in docs/receipts/verify-ledger.json, a residue of 2, and 0 citing nothing anywhere. The residue is campaign-close-verify-p4-batch, whose verdict lives in a commit body and whose range no verifier ever reached, and the tag of the closeout lane writing this line. What closed the gap was neither branch of the question: the campaign's rendered R-35 verdicts were transcribed out of the orchestration journals, which is the ledger's own `backfill` and `residue_sweep` route and is a transcription of verifiers' artifacts rather than a reading of the clause. The question is untouched: both branches stand exactly as written, and whether the clause binds the campaign's past is still the owner's to say. What has changed is only what it would cost -- the backwards branch now buys 2 passes rather than 61 -- and a cost is not an answer. 'The residue is campaign-close-verify-p4-batch, whose verdict lives in a commit body and whose range no verifier ever reached' is two claims and only the second holds. What is true is the derived flag -- verify-backlog.json's row reads cites_an_r35_answer_in_a_commit_body true -- and the derivation (tests/test_verify_ledger.py::_groups_citing_a_verdict_in_a_commit_body) is a conjunction over the group's own commit bodies, a mechanism name AND a verdict word, which 209da2f satisfies because it transcribes R-35 verdicts about six OTHER slices. The ledger's coverage block already names this limitation in a_groups_own_next_commit_can_flip_its_citation_state: 'what the derivation cannot do is tell WHOSE answer a body carries'. The sentence stays written and the measurement stands beside it; nothing about the owed ruling moves, and the residue's size is unchanged by the correction. Anchored 2026-08-17, and this correction is the third the field has taken for one reason: 'Measured on this tip' names no tip. Every figure in that sentence -- 125 slice tags, 123 with a verdict, a residue of 2, 0 citing nothing anywhere -- was true of b02e4ca, the commit that wrote it, and false of the next tip that shipped a slice group. 6a357b4 took the tag total to 126 and the residue to 3, e4338b7 took the covered count to 124 and swapped the residue's membership, and round 129 moved it again. The sentence's membership clause dates the same way: at b02e4ca the residue was campaign-close-verify-p4-batch and campaign-close-final-integration, which was then 'the tag of the closeout lane writing this line'. So the reading is anchored where the close report anchors its own dated readings -- at the commit that stated it, read out of git -- and tests/test_rulings_owed.py re-derives all four figures from `git show b02e4ca:docs/receipts/verify-ledger.json`, with R-05's red beside them. The tip's readings are not restated here at all: live_figures below names the artifact and the path that owns each one, which is the gap ledger's own rule -- a value here would be the second home criterion 4 exists to forbid. What this does not do is re-word anything: the promise this field made when it was written, 'so this field cannot be the second home that goes stale a second time', was broken inside the lane that made it, and it was an R-35 verifier that found it (round 129, campaign-close-final-integration-r35/unmentioned-3) rather than a reader. The promise stays written, the way it failed stays written, and what changed is the mechanism under it.

measurement_anchor.what_it_anchors: The four figures what_the_measurement_now_reads states and its membership clause. They were readings of that commit's tip and a reading of a tip stops being one the moment another slice group ships, which this campaign expects rather than treats as a defect.

live_figures.rule: The tip's readings, named rather than restated. Each names the artifact and the dotted path that owns it and tests/test_rulings_owed.py resolves each one at run time, so this row cannot state a figure the measurement artifact contradicts. read_as says how the path is read: a value is the number itself, a length is the size of the list there.

answered.what_else_the_same_ruling_must_settle: Added 2026-08-17, and it is a hole in the population rather than a second question. The clause's denominator is derived from the trailing parenthetical of a commit subject, and the commits in the campaign range that carry none are outside it -- the count is live_figures' commits_outside_the_denominator, read from the ledger's coverage block, and the block reports them rather than dropping them, which is why nothing here is hidden. What is unsettled is what they ARE. Either an untagged commit belongs to no slice, in which case 'every slice' never quantified over it and the denominator is right as it stands; or the tag convention was not universal, in which case those commits belong to slices whose verdicts the clause does ask for and the denominator is short by an unknown amount. That is the same question the first clause asks -- what the clause's unit is -- so it is ruled with it and by the same owner, rather than being filed as a gap of its own that could be closed by somebody adopting a reading. A certification reviewer raised it as a minor on 2026-08-17 and asked exactly this: that it be named to whoever rules. What a lane may not do about it is what it may not do about the clause, one step earlier: it may not retro-tag a commit subject, because rewriting subjects rewrites the history the denominator is derived from and is the third refused shortcut wearing a different hat; and it may not declare the untagged commits 'not really slices', which is the same shortcut said out loud. Both branches leave the counter exactly where it is until the ruling comes. Settled 2026-08-18 by the fifth ruling of the owner's ruling this row closed on, and settled the way the field says it had to be: by the same owner and with the clause, rather than by a lane adopting a reading. Both arms of the question are answered rather than one being chosen -- an untagged commit that touches no behaviour is outside 'every slice' and owes nothing, and an untagged commit that touches src/ belongs to work the clause does ask about. The second arm is no longer an unknown amount: it is enumerated, derived from the tree on every run, in the measurement artifact's own coverage block under untagged_commits_that_touch_src, and its size is named in live_figures rather than stated here for the reason this field already gives. Each enumerated row owes a batch verdict naming its range or a dated acceptance note, every row is uncovered today and the block's counter says so, and landing those verdicts is scheduled work rather than a hole. Retro-tagging stays refused, in the enumeration's own words as well as in this field's.
answered.the_cost_of_deciding_late: Added 2026-08-17, and it is an argument about WHEN this row is worth answering rather than about which way. It carries nothing new about the question; what it carries is a mechanism that had never been written where whoever rules would read it. Two parts, and the second is the certification reviewer's own. First, the branch count: the question above offers two branches and there is a third, measured on 2026-08-16 and recorded in the close report's section 16.3 and in campaign-gap-ledger.json's G14 blocker -- rule that a group's verdict may be recorded by a commit carrying that same group's tag. It is named here because a branch a reader has to find in a report section is a branch the ruler does not have, and because it is the only one of the three that TERMINATES: recording a verdict is itself a commit, every commit carries a slice tag, and a tag with no verdict is residue, so under either of the first two branches the act of closing the residue creates residue. Second, what four certification passes have now measured about that mechanism: every slice group to enter the residue since round 129 is a certification pass answering a review of this very question, so the process convened to grade the clause is currently the ONLY thing adding to what it grades. The residue's size is live_figures' residue and its membership is the ledger's own list; neither is restated here, which is what keeps this field from becoming the second home the field above it broke twice. The consequence is a property rather than a number: while the clause's unit is unruled, each further review round moves the clause further from discharge by exactly one tag, and it does so however well anybody works. That is a reason to decide soon and it is not a reason to decide either way. What a lane may not do is unchanged and is the whole point of writing this down rather than acting on it: a lane may not adopt the third branch because it terminates, may not adopt the forward reading because the residue is inconvenient, and may not stop recording its own passes to keep the counter still -- an unrecorded pass is the residue hidden rather than closed, which is the failure shape this campaign exists to remove wearing the campaign's own uniform.
answered.why_this_one_is_recorded_as_an_owners_ru: Every row above closed by an amendment -- the orchestration re-reading its own contract on a ground it had measured, which is a decision a lane could in principle have reached and which this ledger's own why_a_lane_may_not_write_these says the umbrella's owner records. This one could not close that way and said so from the day it opened: both branches it offered were a lane deciding what a criterion means, and the third the close report later measured was a lane deciding that its own tag need not be verified. So the umbrella gains a section of its own -- Owner's rulings -- and the ruling is transcribed there by the lane that received it rather than authored by it. The distinction is kept in the tree rather than in anybody's memory, so a reader can tell which of the campaign's conclusions the campaign was entitled to draw.

why_the_answered_rows_stay: A closed row keeps its question, its measurement artifact and what the ruling unblocked. Deleting it would leave the amendment standing in the umbrella with no record of what it was answering, which is the shape -- a conclusion whose question nobody can recover -- this campaign spent four hundred commits removing.
